sections.content_markdown: $$ \text{ZnSO}_4 + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\quad\quad\quad} \text{ZnSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O} $$ $$ \text{Heptahydrate Zinc Sulfate} $$ $$ \text{FeSO}_4 + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\quad\quad\quad} \text{FeSO}_4 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O} $$ $$ \text{Heptahydrate Ferrous Sulfate} $$ $$ \text{CaCl}_2 + 6\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\quad\quad\quad} \text{CaCl}_2 \cdot 6\text{H}_2\text{O} $$ $$ \text{Hexahydrate Calcium Chloride} $$ $$ \text{MgCl}_2 + 7\text{H}_2\text{O} \xrightarrow{\quad\quad\quad} \text{MgCl}_2 \cdot 7\text{H}_2\text{O} $$ $$ \text{Heptahydrate Magnesium Chloride} $$  A hydration reaction is basically similar to an addition reaction. However, in addition reactions, there is electron exchange while in hydration, there is none.

**Isomerization Reaction:** Two compounds with similar molecular formula but with different properties are called isomers of each other. A chemical reaction in which atoms in a molecule rearrange themselves to form one isomer from another isomer is called isomerization. For example, $\text{H}_4\text{N}_2\text{CO}$ molecular formula denotes two compounds with varied structural formula: $\text{NH}_4\text{CNO}$ (ammonium cyanate) and urea ($\text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CO}-\text{NH}_2$). They are isomers of each other. When heat is applied to ammonium cyanate, it produces urea.  $$ \text{NH}_4\text{CNO} \xrightarrow{\text{Heat}} \text{H}_2\text{N}-\text{CO}-\text{NH}_2 $$

**Polymerization Reaction:** A large number of molecules of the same compound combine together to form a large molecule of heavy atomic mass, at high temperature and pressure and in the presence of a catalyst. This reaction is called polymerization. In such cases, the large molecule is called a polymer and each of the smaller molecules that combine together are called monomers. Under the effect of 1200 atm. pressure, $200^\circ\text{C}$ temperature and $\text{O}_2$ catalyst, numerous smaller molecules of ethylene combine into a large polymer molecule of polythene. This reaction is polymerization reaction of ethylene. Here, ethylene molecules are the monomers while polythene molecule is the polymer. In the equation, $n$ denotes the number of molecules.  $$ n(\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2) \xrightarrow[200^\circ\text{C}, 1200 \text{ atm}]{\text{O}_2} (-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-)_n $$
